sources.title: Nikolay Kradin: From Tribal Confederation to Empire, the Evolution of Rouran Society (2005)
sources.note: Direct scholarly PDF read, especially printed 149 to 150, 154 to 156, 158 to 160 and 166 to 167. Shelun 402, military organization, diplomacy and 552 to 555 dissolution. Older claim of virtually no archaeology is superseded by newer studies in this packet. No adoption of derogatory descriptions or categorical ethnic-language identifications.

sources.title: Kürşat and Elvin Yıldırım: Cultural and Social Structure in the Rourans (2024)
sources.note: Direct Bilig 110, pages 157 to 178, DOI 10.12995/bilig.11007. Pages 168 to 170 for felt homes, Mumo and farming request; pages 161 to 162 for changing recording practices. Page 170 cites the Chinese seed-grain phrase explicitly. Source criticisms retained; speculative monotheism and shamans-as-medicine generalizations not adopted.

sources.title: Jamsranjav Bayarsaikhan and colleagues: Origins of saddles and riding technology in East Asia (2024)
sources.note: Direct Antiquity article, DOI 10.15184/aqy.2023.172, Urd Ulaan Uneet burial, Results and Discussion read. Local manufacture interpreted from birch and horsehide; calibrated strap date 267 to 535 CE, not a precise 420 manufacture year. Horse intensively ridden, no recovered stirrups from saddle itself; Khukh Nuur has a separate iron stirrup. Political causal link remains hypothesis.

sources.title: Nikolai Seregin and colleagues: Dating the Rouran-period cemetery of Choburak-I (2024)
sources.note: Direct Radiocarbon article, DOI 10.1017/RDC.2024.72. Abstract, Discussion/Conclusion and Appendix 1 fully consulted. Modeled cemetery 318 to 402 cal CE (95.4%), principally earlier than map interval; no ethnic certainty inferred. Kurgans 29a, 32a and 34 for comb, sewing/spinning equipment, horse equipment and catalogued hygienic brush.

sources.title: Zhang Naizhu: Non-Han communities of late Northern Wei Luoyang (2018)
sources.note: Original scholarly article, Journal of Shihezi University 32(5), pages 74 to 85, hosted by Shanxi University. Direct PDF failed; indexed original printed page 79 read in full. Quotes Princess Chidilian’s Chinese epitaph, including 尊重师傅，访问诗史 and death in Wuding year 8 at age thirteen. Exact query: "尊重师傅" "北魏晚期洛阳地区". Modern printed transcription; English phrase is our literal translation.

sources.title: Zhang Qingjie: Foreign merchants and their trade in Northern Dynasties China (2006)
sources.note: Direct Science Press original chapter preview in 4th to 6th Century North China and Eurasia, printed page 25/PDF page 30. Princess Ruru’s resting pottery camel carries tent equipment and silk; explicit citation to Cixian 1984 excavation report. No political provenance inferred for all cargo or universal household claim.

sources.title: Alexander Savelyev and Choongwon Jeong: Early nomads of the Eastern Steppe and tentative western connections (2020)
sources.note: Direct Evolutionary Human Sciences paper, section 3.1 for political end and diverse population; section 3.2/page 10 for later Bugut and Khuis Tolgoi dating and limits of linguistic inference. Its pre-2022 genetic conclusions are not used; newer study cited separately.

sources.title: Max Planck Society: Origins of the Avars elucidated with ancient DNA (2022)
sources.note: Direct original research-institution report of Gnecchi-Ruscone et al., Cell 2022. Northeast Asian origins of sampled Avar elites and likely migration after Rouran collapse, with heterogeneous European populations. No identity equated mechanically with ancestry.

proposedOverrides.name: Rouran Khaganate (Ruanruan)
proposedOverrides.summary: A powerful Mongolian steppe confederation, the Rouran were defeated in the 550s despite the map’s later endpoint.

batchIdentityNotes.identity: Exact HB record Ruanruan, from 400 to 600. Rouran is a spelling of the same historical confederation; no second indexed ID associated.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Two identical precision-1 snapshots, world-400.json and world-500.json, bbox [73.435,42.271,116.319,53.467]. Broad geographic outline does not prove precise control.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: Shelun khagan title 402; defeat 552 to 555; public period after 555 explicitly an imported overhang. Choburak-I 318 to 402 is earlier regional context. Saddle direct date spans 267 to 535; no midpoint point-year.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Chinese epitaph of Rouran princess at Eastern Wei court, 550, exact modern scholarly transcription. No native Rouran inscription invented or later Khuis Tolgoi backdated.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: Chronicles can be hostile; no adoption of insults as hygiene evidence. No precise ordinary-home sanitation or clinical medicine claim. Cemetery objects are regional contextual evidence, not certainty of imperial allegiance. Avar migration evidence concerns sampled elites, not a one-to-one identity of peoples.
